scams.name: Mérida Airport (MID) Taxi & Pre-Paid-Only Overcharge Scam
scams.description: Mérida Airport (MID) is Yucatán's main gateway — small, efficient, 10 km from Centro Histórico (20 min drive) — but arrivals-kerb touts exploit the pre-paid-only taxi system. Traveler reports cover airport-to-Centro logistics, pickup-rules, and a specific 2025 Uber-availability quirk at MID. The legitimate fare: MID airport to Centro Histórico is MX$275–$350 via the official Transporte Terrestre prepaid booth inside arrivals; Uber is available BUT with limited airport pickup (Uber-Mérida has policy differences vs other cities); typical Uber rate MX$180–$250 if pickup works. The 2025 scams: (a) 'premium taxi' kiosks inside arrivals quoting MX$500–$800 flat rate (2–3x real Transporte Terrestre rate); (b) claim 'Uber doesn't work at MID' — Uber DOES work, but with meet-at-parking-lot-P2 limitation per traveler reports; (c) arrivals-kerb 'hotel transfer' sign-holders at 2–3x real rate; (d) 'combined airport + Chichén Itzá day tour' bundled at MX$3,500 with excuse 'it's easier just one booking' — tour commission padded 80%+; (e) return-trip 'night surcharge' at MX$600 for departures before 6 AM (no such legitimate surcharge exists). For older travelers: (1) use the official Transporte Terrestre booth inside arrivals — MX$275–$350 flat-rate prepaid with printed receipt; this IS the safest 2025 option per community consensus; (2) Uber IS an option but meet driver at parking level P2 (not curb) — traveler reports document the specific limitation; typical fare MX$180–$250 but drivers sometimes cancel; Transporte Terrestre is more reliable; (3) IGNORE every 'premium taxi' kiosk at MX$500+; (4) if your hotel offers free airport pickup (common for Casa Lecanda, Hacienda Xcanatún, Rosas & Xocolate), use it; (5) budget shared combi to Centro runs MX$30 per person from terminal exit — 40 min with stops; (6) NEVER bundle the airport transfer with a Chichén Itzá tour — these are separate purchases; (7) for return, pre-book Transporte Terrestre at the hotel 24 hours ahead, MX$275–$350 same rate; (8) MID is tiny and navigable — no need for 'VIP express service' add-ons.
scams.avoidance: Official Transporte Terrestre booth inside arrivals: MX$275–$350 Uber works at MID but meet at parking P2, not curb (sometimes cancels) Use hotel free airport pickup (most boutique hotels include) Budget: combi shared van MX$30 per person (40 min) NEVER bundle airport with Chichén Itzá tour — separate purchases
scams.location: Mérida Manuel Crescencio Rejón Airport (MID) arrivals, Terminal 1 taxi counter, 'sitio pre-paid' kiosks, Centro Histórico hotel drop-offs

scams.name: Chichén Itzá 'Skip-the-Line' Ticket Fraud & Parking Shakedown
scams.description: Chichén Itzá is Yucatán's #1 UNESCO draw and hosts Mexico's most-documented 2025 entrance-scam ecosystem. Traveler reports warn travelers not to buy tickets from touts on the Chichén Itzá approach, document 2025 vendor aggression at the site, and trace the broader tourist-trap evolution over the past two decades. The legitimate cost (2025): entry is MX$614 for foreigners total (MX$90 INAH federal + MX$524 Yucatán state) — split across two separate counters. NO 'skip-the-line' ticket exists; the queue at 8 AM opening is 5–15 min. Parking at the OFFICIAL lot is MX$80 (24-hour). The 2025 scams: (a) 'skip-the-line Chichén Itzá' tickets sold online at MX$1,500–$2,500 — either fake barcodes or regular tickets at 2–4x markup; (b) roadside 'park here cheap' touts on Route 180 approaching Pisté town — forced parking fees MX$200–$300 far from official entry, then 'shuttle' charges MX$100/person; (c) 'mandatory guide MX$800 per person' at entrance — no guide required; optional licensed guides charge MX$800–$1,200 PER GROUP (4–8 people); (d) 'combined INAH + state ticket' resellers at MX$800+ (you still pay separate counter fees anyway); (e) post-pyramid souvenir 'carvings' at MX$2,000–$5,000 claimed as 'Mayan artisan'; mass-produced identical items sell for MX$200–$500 at Mérida craft markets; (f) fake 'Cenote Ik Kil combined ticket' resold at 2x rate. For older travelers: (1) book Chichén Itzá entry via official INAH website (boletomuseo.inah.gob.mx) OR pay at the gate — MX$614 total foreigner rate; NO skip-the-line upgrade exists; (2) park ONLY at the OFFICIAL lot MX$80 — ignore every roadside 'park here' tout; (3) NO mandatory guide — optional guides MX$800–$1,200 PER GROUP of 4–8 people; most travelers self-guide with the free INAH app (English + Spanish); (4) arrive at 8 AM opening — by 11 AM tour buses from Cancún/Playa swell the crowd 10x; (5) bring sun protection (no shade inside complex), water, bug spray; summer 35°C+ heat is dangerous for older travelers; (6) for a combined Cenote Ik Kil visit, go DIRECTLY to Ik Kil (MX$180 entry) and NOT via resellers; (7) souvenirs: buy at Mérida's Mercado de Artesanías García Rejón (Calle 65) at 1/10th the site prices; (8) if driving from Mérida, use the CUOTA (toll road, MX$420 each way) — faster, safer than the LIBRE (free) road per community consensus.
scams.avoidance: Book via boletomuseo.inah.gob.mx OR pay at gate: MX$614 total Park at OFFICIAL lot MX$80 — ignore every roadside tout NO mandatory guide; optional MX$800–$1,200 PER GROUP (4–8) Arrive at 8 AM opening — tour buses flood by 11 AM Use CUOTA (toll) road from Mérida, not free LIBRE
scams.location: Chichén Itzá UNESCO site entrance, Highway 180 (Mérida–Cancún) approach, Pisté town parking zones, Libre vs Cuota road turnoffs

scams.name: Mi Lindo Yucatán / Highway Restaurant Forced-Stop Bait-and-Switch
scams.description: 'Mi Lindo Yucatán' is a specific highway restaurant on the Mérida–Chichén Itzá–Valladolid corridor that has become the canonical named anchor for a 2025 tourist-trap pattern targeting tour buses and rental-car drivers. Traveler reports flag 'Mi Lindo Yucatán' directly as a scam warning and document related scams on the way to Chichén Itzá including parking touts. Broader traveler reports also track the 2025 vendor ecosystem around the site. The 2025 scam pattern: (a) tour-bus driver OR tour-company kickback where rental-car tourists are explicitly directed to 'Mi Lindo Yucatán' (or similar named restaurants: Mesón del Marqués, Rancho Yucateco, etc.) with 'cultural demo included'; (b) on arrival, the 'free cochinita pibil demonstration' is 15 min of pre-show, then MX$350–$600 lunch (vs MX$150–$250 fair price at authentic Valladolid restaurants); (c) 'tequila demonstration' upsells MX$800 bottles; (d) 'traditional Mayan craft' shop attached at 3–5x market prices; (e) tour bus 'scheduled stop 45 min' that stretches to 75–90 min while drivers earn commission; (f) credit-card cloning at cashier with 'demo swipe'; (g) fake 'buy 2 get 1 free' tequila deals where the 'free' bottle was the one you paid MX$600 markup for. For older travelers: (1) if driving rental car, DO NOT stop at any 'recommended' highway restaurant on Route 180 between Mérida and Chichén Itzá — eat in Valladolid at authentic Yucatec spots (Yerbabuena del Sisal, Conato 1910, Meson del Marqués); (2) if on a tour bus and forced-stop occurs, you can decline lunch — bring snacks and drinks to eat outside; (3) book tours ONLY through Google 4.7+ operators with 'no commission stops' explicitly promised in writing: Jugo Cenote Experiences, Yuchitur Aventura, or Ki'op Mérida; (4) avoid the 'combined Chichén Itzá + cenote + lunch' package tours — these ALWAYS include commission stops; (5) in Valladolid, Yerbabuena del Sisal (Calle 41) does authentic Yucatec cochinita pibil at MX$150–$250 per person — 100x better than highway traps; (6) NEVER swipe your credit card at 'demo' counters — pay cash for souvenirs; (7) for a real Mayan cultural experience, visit Ek' Balam community cooperative near Valladolid — entry MX$150, authentic ruins, no commission pressure; (8) traveler reports list specific vendor-name warnings worth saving.
scams.avoidance: DON'T stop at highway 'recommended' restaurants on Route 180 Eat in Valladolid: Yerbabuena del Sisal, Conato 1910, Meson del Marqués Book tours with 'no commission stops' in writing Avoid 'combined Chichén + cenote + lunch' packages NEVER swipe card at 'demo' counters — pay cash for souvenirs
scams.location: Highway 180 Libre (Mérida–Valladolid–Cancún), Pisté town approach, Chichén Itzá return trips, Uxmal route highway

scams.name: Mérida Cenote Tour Unlicensed Operator & 'Private Access' Fee Padding
scams.description: Yucatán's cenotes (natural freshwater sinkholes) are Mérida's second-biggest draw after Chichén Itzá. Traveler reports in 2025 extensively cover which cenotes are great and which to avoid, and document the broader 2025 vendor-aggression pattern that extends from Chichén Itzá to cenote tours. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) unlicensed tour operators selling 'private cenote access MX$1,800 per person' when public community cooperative cenotes (Yokdzonot, Cuzamá, San Antonio Mulix) cost MX$150–$250 entry; (b) 'VIP guide + float + photo package MX$2,500' bundled for a Rp 350K activity — floats and public access are included at community-run cenotes; (c) fake 'Mayan shaman cleansing MX$800' at cenote entry — no such cultural requirement exists; (d) 'exclusive Dos Ojos access MX$1,500' when standard entry is MX$350; (e) 'mandatory life-jacket rental MX$200' at community cenotes where jackets are INCLUDED in entry; (f) 'commission restaurants' added to tour route padding 1–2 hours of unwanted shopping. Traveler reports cover the broader 2025 Yucatán-tourist context including police concerns. For older travelers: (1) visit community-cooperative cenotes — the BEST experiences in 2025 — Yokdzonot (MX$150), San Antonio Mulix (3 cenotes MX$450 combo), Cuzamá horse-cart cenote tour (MX$300); fees go to local communities, experiences are uncrowded; (2) book tours ONLY via Google 4.7+ operators: Yuchitur Aventura, Ki'op Mérida, Cenote Cascada, or Zamná Tours — MX$800–$1,500 per person day trip to 3 cenotes with lunch; (3) REFUSE every 'VIP private access', 'shaman cleansing', 'life-jacket rental surcharge' offer; (4) driving yourself: rent from Hertz/Europcar airport, use CUOTA where available, bring MX$150–$450 per cenote in small bills; (5) for older travelers with mobility concerns: Ik Kil has stairs but also a platform; Yokdzonot has a ramp; San Antonio Mulix has easier ground-level access; (6) bring biodegradable sunscreen ONLY — chemical sunscreens damage cenote ecosystems and some sites require rinse-off; (7) avoid weekends at Ik Kil (tour-bus crush); mid-week early-AM is best; (8) traveler reports list recommendations for which cenotes to visit and which to avoid in detail.
scams.avoidance: Community cenotes: Yokdzonot MX$150, San Antonio Mulix MX$450, Cuzamá MX$300 Book Yuchitur Aventura, Ki'op Mérida (Google 4.7+) MX$800–$1,500 REFUSE all 'VIP', 'shaman', 'life-jacket surcharge' demands Bring MX$150–$450 per cenote in small bills Biodegradable sunscreen only; avoid weekends at Ik Kil
scams.location: Cenote Ik Kil, Dos Ojos, X'keken, Saamal, Yokdzonot community cooperative, San Antonio Mulix ring road, Ruta de los Cenotes approach

scams.name: Mérida Mundo Maya & Centro Histórico Craft-Shop 'Authentic' Fake-Pricing
scams.description: Mérida's Centro Histórico has a 2025 craft-shop ecosystem where tourists are sold mass-produced goods as 'authentic Mayan artisan' at 3–10x fair prices. One 2025 first-person account documents a specific Calle 60 shop ('Mundo Maya Store Merida') with overpriced 'cooperative' branding. Traveler reports also cover the highway-restaurant parallel pattern (Mi Lindo Yucatán) and the adjacent UNESCO-site vendor pattern at Chichén Itzá. The 2025 scams: (a) Calle 60 'authentic cooperative' shops selling identical 'Mayan woven goods' at MX$1,500–$4,000 per item — same items at Mercado Municipal García Rejón (Calle 65) are MX$200–$600; (b) 'limited edition amber jewelry MX$3,500' that's actually copal resin (different, lower-value) or dyed plastic; (c) 'hammock handmade by Mayan women MX$2,500' for mass-produced versions — genuine hand-woven hammocks from Tixkokob cooperatives are MX$600–$1,800 at the village; (d) 'ethical tequila/mezcal bottle MX$2,000' with generic labels (genuine certified spirits cost MX$400–$1,200 at reputable liquor stores); (e) 'Cuban cigar authentic MX$1,500' at Mérida kiosks — Cuban cigars imported to Mexico legally cost MX$200–$600 per single at tobacco specialty shops; (f) credit-card cloning at commission shops using 'manual entry' devices. For older travelers: (1) shop ONLY at Mérida's Mercado Municipal García Rejón (Calle 65 × 56) for general crafts — transparent prices, haggling expected, MX$200–$600 for quality goods; (2) for hammocks, go DIRECTLY to Tixkokob village (25 km east of Mérida) where family cooperatives weave authentic hand-made hammocks MX$600–$1,800; (3) for amber/copal jewelry, shop at Mercado García Rejón or reputable Chiapas amber dealers — ask for 'amber' (not copal) and verify with UV light (amber glows blue); (4) REFUSE every 'authentic Mayan cooperative' shop on Calle 60 Paseo de Montejo tourist corridor — these are commission shops; (5) NEVER use credit card 'manual entry' at craft shops — pay cash or refuse; (6) for mezcal/tequila, Casa Cozumel Liquor or Liverpool Mérida supermarket have authentic bottles at transparent prices; (7) traveler reports list specific store-name warnings worth saving; (8) when in doubt, comparison-shop the same item at Mercado García Rejón before buying from any Calle 60 'cooperative'.
scams.avoidance: Shop at Mercado Municipal García Rejón (Calle 65 × 56) with haggling Hammocks: go to Tixkokob village cooperatives MX$600–$1,800 Amber: verify with UV (amber glows blue, copal doesn't) REFUSE 'authentic Mayan cooperative' shops on Calle 60 tourist corridor Comparison-shop at García Rejón before any Calle 60 purchase
scams.location: Mundo Maya Store (Calle 60), Paseo de Montejo commission shops, Centro Histórico artisan souvenir shops, Chichén Itzá 'on the way' stops

scams.name: Progreso Cruise Port Taxi & Artisan-Shop Commission Scam
scams.description: Progreso is Yucatán's main cruise port (35 km north of Mérida) and hosts a 2025 cruise-tourist-targeting ecosystem. Traveler reports cover the local beach-club landscape, water clarity at Progreso-area beaches, 2025 solo-traveler advice for beaches around Mérida, and a historical note from 2019 when cruise-ship arrivals to Progreso were suspended for two months. The 2025 scams: (a) 'free shuttle to Centro' at the cruise pier that ends at a commission craft shop, not the town center; (b) 'Mérida day tour' booked at pier at MX$3,500–$6,000 per person when Mérida is just 35 km away (1 hour drive) and Uber round-trip is MX$600–$900; (c) beach-club 'VIP chair + towel + bottle MX$2,500 per person' at Malecón — normal pier day pass at reputable clubs (Playa Linda, El Cocos) is MX$400–$800; (d) 'authentic Yucatán lunch + artisan visit' tour at MX$2,200 with 40 min at lunch and 80 min at commission shop; (e) 'Uxmal ruins combined with beach' at MX$4,500 — combined tours with drive time leave 45 min at each site; (f) Progreso pier taxi quoting MX$1,500 to Mérida (real MX$450–$600 metered, MX$300 via Uber from Progreso Centro). For older travelers (cruise-day visitors): (1) SKIP the 'free shuttle' — walk 10 min from pier to Progreso town center (free, direct); (2) if going to Mérida, book Uber from Progreso town center (not pier) MX$300–$400 one-way; (3) for a real Yucatán experience on a cruise day, CHOOSE ONE: Mérida Centro Histórico OR Uxmal OR a cenote — don't cram; (4) if Mérida, Uber round-trip MX$600–$900 + Centro walking is sufficient for 4-hour visit; (5) for Uxmal ruins (75 km from Progreso), book an independent licensed guide via GetYourGuide or Viator at MX$1,200–$1,800 per person (vs cruise-pier MX$4,500); (6) beach-day at Progreso: Playa Linda or El Cocos have fair day passes MX$400–$800 — skip the 'VIP MX$2,500' upsells; (7) NEVER pay MX$1,500+ for Progreso-to-Mérida taxi — Uber works throughout Yucatán; (8) allow 90 min buffer back to ship departure — Progreso traffic on cruise days can be heavy.
scams.avoidance: Skip 'free shuttle' — walk 10 min from pier to Progreso town Uber from Progreso town to Mérida: MX$300–$400 one-way Choose ONE: Mérida, Uxmal, OR cenote — don't cram cruise day Independent Uxmal guide via GetYourGuide MX$1,200–$1,800 Allow 90 min buffer to ship departure
scams.location: Progreso cruise pier (Malecón), Terminal Turístico, 'free shuttle' to Centro, Malecón beach clubs, Progreso town commission shops
